provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Disease and prevention
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list ways diseases spread.
The pupils should be able to state three prevention habits.
Introduction:
We have all been sick before. Today we learn how not to get sick.
Content:
Diseases spread through coughs, dirty hands and sharing food. We prevent sickness by washing hands with soap. We cover our mouths when we cough. We eat clean food from clean plates.
Class activity:
Let's pretend to sneeze into our elbows. Let's wash our hands with soap and water.
Evaluation questions:
How do diseases spread? What should we do before eating? How do we cover our cough?
Summary:
We must wash our hands to stay healthy.

topics.title: Malaria and nets
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify a mosquito.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate net hanging.
Introduction:
Mosquitoes make us sick with malaria. We have special nets to keep them away.
Content:
Mosquitoes lay eggs in water. They grow and bite us at night. We sleep under nets to stop mosquito bites. Nets keep us safe from malaria.
Class activity:
Let's practice hanging a net over a small bed. Let's sing a song about mosquitoes.
Evaluation questions:
What do mosquitoes do to us? Where do mosquitoes lay eggs? How do we use nets?
Summary:
Sleeping under nets keeps mosquitoes away.

topics.title: Immunisation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what vaccines do.
The pupils should be able to show their immunisation card.
Introduction:
Sometimes we get special medicine to stop sickness. This is called immunisation.
Content:
Vaccines are special injections. They make our bodies strong against diseases. Our parents keep cards showing our vaccines. We must keep our cards safe.
Class activity:
Let's look at our immunisation cards. Let's pretend to give injections to dolls.
Evaluation questions:
What are vaccines? Why do we need them? Where do we keep our immunisation card?
Summary:
Vaccines keep us from getting sick.

topics.title: Environment and health
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify dirty environments.
The pupils should be able to list three clean environment habits.
Introduction:
Our surroundings can make us sick or keep us healthy. Let's learn about clean environments.
Content:
Dirty gutters and bushes breed mosquitoes. Rubbish attracts rats and flies. We must sweep our compound daily. We must not allow water to stand in containers.
Class activity:
Let's draw posters about clean environments. Let's sweep a small area in class.
Evaluation questions:
What is in dirty environments? What do dirty places breed? What should we do to keep our compound clean?
Summary:
A clean environment keeps us healthy.

topics.title: Water watch
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify safe drinking water.
The pupils should be able to sort water sources.
Introduction:
Water is good for us but some water can make us sick. Let's learn about safe water.
Content:
Safe water is clean and clear. We can get water from taps, wells or boreholes. We must not drink water from ponds or streams. We can boil water to make it safe.
Class activity:
Let's sort pictures of water sources into safe and unsafe. Let's pretend to boil water.
Evaluation questions:
What makes water safe? Where can we get safe water? What can we do to make water safe?
Summary:
We must drink clean water to stay healthy.

topics.title: Food safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate hand washing.
The pupils should be able to identify safe street food.
Introduction:
The food we eat can make us healthy or sick. Let's learn about food safety.
Content:
We must wash our hands before eating. Food should be covered to keep flies away. Street food is not always safe. We must check that food is cooked well.
Class activity:
Let's wash our hands properly. Let's sort food pictures into safe and unsafe.
Evaluation questions:
What should we do before eating? Why should food be covered? Is all street food safe?
Summary:
Clean hands and safe food keep us healthy.

topics.title: Road safety full
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate crossing the road safely.
The pupils should be able to identify traffic lights.
Introduction:
Roads are busy places. We must learn how to stay safe on the road.
Content:
We must look left and right before crossing. We must walk on the pavement. We must not play on the road. Traffic lights tell us when to cross.
Class activity:
Let's practice crossing the road safely. Let's make traffic light crafts.
Evaluation questions:
How do we cross the road safely? Where should we walk? What do traffic lights tell us?
Summary:
We must be careful on the road to stay safe.

topics.title: Stranger and body safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify safe touches.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate what to do with strangers.
Introduction:
Some people might try to harm us. We need to know how to stay safe from strangers.
Content:
Safe touches are on shoulders and back. Unsafe touches are in private areas. If a stranger offers us sweets, we say no. If someone makes us feel uncomfortable, we scream and run to a safe place.
Class activity:
Let's practice saying no to strangers. Let's identify safe and unsafe touches on dolls.
Evaluation questions:
What are safe touches? What should we do with strangers? What do we do if someone makes us feel uncomfortable?
Summary:
We must say no to strangers and unsafe touches.

topics.title: Fire and burn safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify hot objects.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate stop, drop and roll.
Introduction:
Fire and hot things can hurt us. We need to learn how to stay safe from burns.
Content:
Matches, candles and stoves are hot. We must not play with fire. If our clothes catch fire, we stop, drop and roll. We must tell adults about fire.
Class activity:
Let's practice stop, drop and roll. Let's identify hot objects in pictures.
Evaluation questions:
What things are hot? What do we do if our clothes catch fire? Should we play with matches?
Summary:
We must stay away from hot things to avoid burns.

topics.title: Revision and safety quiz
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer safety questions.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate safety practices.
Introduction:
Today we will revise all we have learned about staying safe and healthy.
Content:
We have learned about disease prevention, malaria nets, immunisation, clean environments, safe water, food safety, road safety, stranger safety and fire safety. All these help us stay healthy and safe.
Class activity:
Let's play a safety quiz game. Let's demonstrate what we have learned.
Evaluation questions:
How do we prevent malaria? What should we do with strangers? How do we cross the road safely?
Summary:
We know many ways to stay safe and healthy.
